Computer science.title: MindExplore+: Towards Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action System
Computer science.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
Computer science.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) is crucial for autonomous decision-making in embodied systems. While current methods have advanced single-skill abilities, their short-horizon capability limits applicability in real-world scenarios. To address this challenge, we propose MindExplore+, a hierarchical VLA system with cross-skill capabilities for long-horizon tasks in dynamic environments. By iteratively aligning task planning and action execution, this approach ensures excellent generalization across diverse real-world scenarios. In the reasoning layer, task specific chains of thought (CoT) are designed for planning long horizon task sequences and providing meta-action signals. In the acting layer, a simple but powerful Mixture of Policy Experts strategy is built inspired by signals and multimodal inputs for adaptively selecting skill experts and generating closed-loop action sequences. Computer science.title: Text-to-Image Diffusion Sample Selector for Learning With Noisy Labels
Computer science.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
Computer science.abstract: Large-scale datasets inevitably contain noisy labels, compelling deep neural networks to overfit and degrade in performance. Existing learning with noisy labels (LNL) approaches partially alleviate this through sample selection. However, selection processes themselves inherently rely on models trained on noisy data, which makes them prone to self-confirmation bias. To overcome this issue, we decouple sample selection from model training by proposing a Text-to-Image Diffusion Sample Selector (TIDS), which can provide a clean initial subset for downstream learning, even under various complex and extremely noisy conditions. Theoretically, we constrain the selection criteria by minimizing the generalization error bound in noisy environments to ensure the reliability of the selected samples and facilitate the effective training of robust models. Our proposed TIDS innovatively explores the…

Computer science.title: Helios: Real Real-Time Long Video Generation Model
Computer science.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
Computer science.abstract: We introduce Helios, the first 14B video generation model that runs at 19.5 FPS on a single NVIDIA H100 GPU and supports minute-scale generation while matching the quality of a strong baseline. We make breakthroughs along three key dimensions: (1) robustness to long-video drifting without commonly used anti-drifting heuristics such as self-forcing, errorbanks, or keyframe sampling; (2) real-time generation without standard acceleration techniques such as KV-cache, sparse/linear attention, or quantization; and (3) training without parallelism or sharding frameworks, enabling image-diffusion-scale batch sizes while fitting up to four 14B models within 80 GB of GPU memory. Specifically, Helios is a 14B autoregressive diffusion model with a unified input representation that natively supports T2V, I2V, and V2V tasks. Computer science.title: RAD-2: Scaling Reinforcement Learning in a Generator-Discriminator Framework
Computer science.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
Computer science.abstract: High-level autonomous driving requires motion planners capable of modeling multimodal future uncertainties while remaining robust in closed-loop interactions. Although diffusion-based planners are effective at modeling complex trajectory distributions, they often suffer from stochastic instabilities and the lack of corrective negative feedback when trained purely with imitation learning. To address these issues, we propose RAD-2, a unified generator-discriminator framework for closed-loop planning. Specifically, a diffusion-based generator is used to produce diverse trajectory candidates, while an RL-optimized discriminator reranks these candidates according to their long-term driving quality. Computer science.title: SparScene: Efficient Traffic Scene Representation via Sparse Graph Learning for Large-Scale Trajectory Generation
Computer science.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
Computer science.abstract: Multi-agent trajectory generation is a core problem for autonomous driving and intelligent transportation systems. However, efficiently modeling the dynamic interactions between numerous road users and infrastructures in complex scenes remains an open problem. Existing methods typically employ distance-based or fully connected dense graph structures to capture interaction information, which not only introduces a large number of redundant edges but also requires complex and heavily parameterized networks for encoding, thereby resulting in low training and inference efficiency, limiting scalability to large and complex traffic scenes. To overcome the limitations of existing methods, we propose SparScene, a sparse graph learning framework designed for efficient and computationally scalable traffic scene representation. Instead of relying on distance thresholds, SparScene leverages the…

Computer science.title: Reasoning Beyond Prediction: From Data-Driven to Causal Software Engineering
Computer science.journal: Communications of the ACM
Computer science.abstract: Software engineering is an intellectually demanding, creative discipline that juggles a web of interdependent tasks to design, build, and assure the quality of increasingly complex systems. As our expectations from software soar—with demands spanning AI-driven products, pervasively distributed and cloud-native architectures, and deeply embedded cyber-physical environments—its complexity steadily increases. In response, a new wave of co-engineering methods and tools, fueled by deep learning, has emerged to augment the process, enhancing automation and decision support. Yet, these advances remain far from delivering the kind of intelligent support that modern software development demands. Computer science.title: An Ethics Ecosystem for AI
Computer science.journal: Communications of the ACM
Computer science.abstract: This article diagnoses ethical failures associated with AI as resulting from the lack of a robust ethics ecosystem . Drawing on the domain of health and healthcare, we identify the components of a functioning ecosystem and explain how an ecosystemic approach helps to manage the scale of the ethical challenges in the domain of AI relative to more typical alternatives.

Psychology.title: Uncovering internal sensory evidence reveals the nature of confidence computation in multi-alternative perceptual decision making.
Psychology.abstract: A central goal of perceptual decision making is to determine the computations underlying choice and confidence in complex, multi-alternative tasks. However, revealing these computations requires knowledge of the internal sensory evidence upon which the computations operate. Unfortunately, unlike for two-choice tasks, there is no established method in multi-alternative tasks to determine how stimuli are transformed into internal sensory evidence. Here we address this critical gap by developing a novel modeling paradigm that reveals how the brain transforms external stimuli into internal sensory evidence during multi-alternative decision making in the context of numerosity tasks. Psychology.title: Older yet faster: Representational development explains accelerated semantic processing in older adults.
Psychology.abstract: Slower responses in older age are often taken as evidence for cognitive decline, yet they may also stem from representational changes shaped by lifelong learning. Building on the information-accumulation perspective on aging, we argue that behavioral change across the lifespan can arise from representational systems continuously updated through learning from the environment. This view predicts that aging may bring both benefits and costs: Performance improves when task demands are congruent with accumulated knowledge but declines when they conflict. We provide convergent evidence for this account across three studies, each comprising the following components. Psychology.title: Causal role of human hippocampus in relational structure learning and inference
Psychology.abstract: When meeting new individuals or known individuals in new circumstances, we intuitively map out their relationships-not merely through direct experience, but by inferring new connections on the basis of prior relational knowledge. How such relational knowledge is represented and used in the brain remains a long-standing question in cognitive neuroscience. Here, using a behavioural task and computational modelling, we show that participants (N = 36) leveraged existing knowledge of relational structures to infer new relationships, facilitating adaptation in changing environments. Whole-brain neuroimaging identified consistent representations of relational structure in the hippocampus. To investigate the causal link between hippocampal representations and inference, we used neural network simulations to predict the behavioural effects of disrupting such representations. Psychology.title: Long-term development of a motor memory
Psychology.abstract: Human behaviour is developed through continuous adaptation to our environment over a range of timescales. Extensive studies have investigated the mechanisms and computations underlying this process of sensorimotor adaptation using several hundred trials. However, most of our motor skills have had countless hours of practice. Here we study a simple motor adaptation task using thousands of training trials over multiple weeks to study the long-term development of a motor memory, and examine changes in adaptation, retention, interlimb transfer, decay, spontaneous recovery and generalization. Unlike previous studies, participants showed near complete compensation to the novel dynamics, along with long-term increases in retention and spontaneous recovery. Psychology.title: A natural field experiment on the effectiveness of economic sanctions before and after the Russian invasion of Ukraine
Psychology.abstract: Here, using two rounds of natural field experiments based on an audit-study approach, we investigated whether sanctioned Russian government officials retain access to the international financial system. Researchers sent 7,081 email solicitations to intermediary firms in 202 countries and jurisdictions to establish shell companies and set up corporate bank accounts. Psychology.title: Surprise Resets the Mind: An Adaptive Online Reset in Working Memory Selection
Psychology.abstract: Human cognition rapidly adapts to unexpected events in dynamic environments, but it remains unclear whether expectation violations rapidly influence the selection of attended information into working memory. Using the attribute-amnesia paradigm, we introduced expectation violations during the surprise trial to test whether unexpected changes improve reporting of a target feature that had been attended and used but was normally not reported. Across six experiments (total N = 250 college students, aged 17–27 years; 149 females), expectation violations reliably improved surprise-trial report of this feature, indicating greater availability in working memory. Psychology.abstract: This preregistered systematic review investigated reciprocal effects between people's self-esteem and the quality of their social relationships by meta-analyzing the available longitudinal data. Analyses were based on 82 samples, including 86,850 participants. Mean age of samples ranged from 8 to 63 years. Humanities and arts.title: Could All Rules Have Goals?
Humanities and arts.abstract: I argue that not all belief-relative normative principles can be represented as requiring the maximization of expected utility. The argument imposes no limits on the distinctions that utility functions can draw, but relies instead on a connection between decision-theoretic representability and uncertainty about one’s own beliefs. By contrast, I argue that evidence-relative normative principles, which say what to do given what would be rational to believe, always admit of such a representation, so long as uncertainty about epistemic rationality is limited in independently plausible ways.

Humanities and arts.title: The Metaphysics of Homelands
Humanities and arts.abstract: National self-determination has an inherently territorial dimension: people who live together in a shared polity require land that can host the population, whose resources can be extracted for the common good, and whose history they find meaningful. This paper explores a particular kind of land that is of distinguished importance in political philosophy: the homeland. Homelands are significant because of the role that is often attributed to them in justifying territorial rights. However, on reflection, the metaphysical nature of homelands is curious. Some of the platitudes we tend to hold about them imply that they resemble large material objects, while others suggest that we should treat them as space-time locations. Humanities and arts.title: Higher‐Order Tense Realism
Humanities and arts.abstract: Realism about tense comes in various forms. In “Tense and Reality” (2005) and “The Reality of Tense” (2006), Kit Fine offered a helpful taxonomy that contributed to shape the current debate on the topic. In our paper “Eternal Facts in an Ageing Universe” (2012), we improved upon this taxonomy, identifying a further type of view that Fine leaves out: Dynamic Absolutism. Both these taxonomies construe the different versions of tense realism in terms of first‐order quantification over facts or states of affairs. Our goal is to show that the logical space of these first‐order tense‐realist positions can be replicated using higher‐order quantification instead. Humanities and arts.title: Aristotle on the Boundaries of Processes
Humanities and arts.abstract: This paper challenges the dominant reading of Aristotle’s theory of the boundaries of processes, according to which he takes every interval of process to be ‘open’, excluding both the beginning and the end. Drawing on the Physics and Metaphysics, I argue that this reading is incorrect. Instead, Aristotle holds that every interval of process is half-open, excluding the end but including the beginning. He also extends this structure to intervals of rest because in both cases the end can (and must) exist without the earlier condition continuing, whereas the beginning cannot exist without the condition it initiates. The alternative reading helps improve our understanding of Aristotle’s handling of the well-known stopping and starting problem, and secures him a defensible place in both ancient and modern debates about boundaries.

Humanities and arts.title: Improving Lives and Avoiding Harm
Humanities and arts.abstract: The Asymmetry in population ethics holds that creating a miserable person is morally impermissible, while not creating a happy person is morally permissible, all else being equal. Harm‐avoidance theories explain the Asymmetry by claiming that, in certain contexts, only actions resulting in harm are impermissible. Two problems threaten these theories: (i) The Problem of Improvable Life Avoidance—requiring agents to avoid creating improvable good lives—and (ii) requiring dominated options. Sophisticated harm‐avoidance theories avoid both problems. However, we show that any harm‐avoidance theory entails either (1) a worse form of The Problem of Improvable Life Avoidance, (2) a troubling form of sadism, (3) an implausibly extreme priority for avoiding a small harm for one person over greater harms for many people, or (4) spurious prohibition dilemmas. Humanities and arts.title: Coal miners as abortionists in Germany, c .1930–1955
Humanities and arts.abstract: Abortion is commonly gendered as a women’s issue. This article centres the role of men in reproductive histories by examining a cohort of twelve coal miners who terminated pregnancies illegally in Germany’s industrial heartland, the Ruhr, between the early 1930s and mid-1950s. The miner-abortionists shed light on two aspects of working-class life: masculinity and community. In a period before the contraceptive pill provided an individualized and feminized method of birth control, working-class men often helped limit their families’ size: birth control was both a material and a gendered issue. For this cohort of coal miners, performing abortions even became an empathetically masculine, boast-worthy skill. Humanities and arts.title: What Is Time?
Humanities and arts.abstract: We argue that time is the great enabler: it is that which makes causation and change possible. We develop this idea into a functionalist account of time that has some very nice features: (i) it differentiates time from space where needed, (ii) it illuminates time via its connection to causation and change, (iii) it accounts for the apparent multiple realizability of time, and (iv) it correctly classifies worlds that have time as such. We compare our account to three rivals: time as the great necessitator, time as the great informer, and time as the measure of change. We show that treating time as an enabler does better.

Humanities and arts.title: Refusing International Debt and the Postcolonial Politics of Yentua in 1970s Ghana
Humanities and arts.abstract: In 1972 the government of Ghana refused to repay loans contracted on the international debt market. As a pivotal moment in the history of decolonization, the policy of Yentua, or ‘We Shall Not Pay’, marked an unprecedented move in Ghana’s relationship with its foreign creditors. Eight years of debt negotiations had exposed the persistence not only of Western financial economic and political control, but also of debt as a mechanism to assert neocolonial power. At the same time, negotiations opened up the possibility of challenging creditors and the continuing relationships of dependency, violence, and extraction. While across Africa the 1970s were marked by increasing economic uncertainty and militarism, this situation did not diminish the will of the Ghanaian public to reimagine the emancipatory potential of debt repudiation. Humanities and arts.title: Bias Against Boltzmann Brains?
Humanities and arts.abstract: A popular indifference principle for self‐locating probability faces skeptical challenges, most notably a skeptical challenge concerning Boltzmann Brains. We examine the prospects for various views that prescribe some degree of bias in place of indifference. Although a bias view has attractive anti‐skeptical features, it turns out that bias leads to puzzles about deference to chance, reflection, and other related principles.

Humanities and arts.title: Substitutional Quantification and Arithmetical Truth
Humanities and arts.abstract: In the mid‐20th century, there was a debate about whether the quantifiers in first‐order logic should be understood objectually or substitutionally. This debate typically focused on ontology and assumed that we could use only one of these two types of quantification. After Kripke and others influentially argued that the two kinds of quantification were logically equivalent, defenses of substitutional quantification were rare. Following Gottlieb and Field, I argue that Kripke was wrong and that substitutional consequence is language‐bound and non‐compact. While of no help with ontology, I also argue that so‐understood, substitutional quantification can be applied to help explain our grasp of a determinate notion of arithmetical truth. To argue for this, I give an account of the metasemantics of the substitutional quantifiers and prove that adding a single, very natural, mixed axiom to…

Humanities and arts.title: Solving the Dual Puzzles of Collective Harm
Humanities and arts.abstract: Suppose some uncoordinated group of agents causes tremendous harm, but none of the individuals could have meaningfully changed this result by acting differently. These “collective harm” cases have been the subject of extended philosophical discussion, but this paper argues that there are really two different, if connected, puzzles presented by such cases: (1) a puzzle about how to characterize the moral injury to those who suffer this harm (the “wrongness puzzle”) and (2) a puzzle about why agents may do something wrong in participating in producing this harm (the “participation puzzle”). This paper elaborates these puzzles, defends the idea that they are different from each other, and offers solutions to them both. Society and law.title: Rising Wages and the Decline of Low-Wage Work
Society and law.abstract: From 2014 to 2024, the share of U.S. hourly workers paid below $15 in real terms fell by two-thirds, from 38 percent to 13 percent. Why? We first distinguish the entry and exit of employers—wherein high-paying employers have supplanted low-paying ones—from organizational changes among incumbent employers. Organizational changes can be imposed on employers by external constraints, like labor market tightness, or emerge from the pursuit of new opportunities. Using panel data drawn from administrative records and job reviews, we bring this framework to bear on the recent wage gains at the bottom of the labor market. Contrary to predictions of creative destruction, we can trace only a small amount of these wage gains to the disappearance of low-wage organizations. Instead, the main driver of rising pay was low- and middle-paying incumbent employers of low-wage occupations increasing pay.…
Society and law.topic: Labor market dynamics and wage inequality

Society and law.title: “Sit Nice!”: Peer Culture, Teacher Capacity, and Joint Socialization Efforts in Preschool
Society and law.abstract: Preschools instill soft skills that are crucial to children’s life outcomes. As preschool access expands, research and policy often focus on improving teacher quality. This focus downplays how much teachers’ efforts may depend on children’s peers. Drawing on two years of ethnography, I highlight two important aspects of socialization: teachers’ capacity to deliver messages in the moment, and peers’ tendency to support those messages. I compare socialization processes at two race- and class-segregated preschools. Three interrelated classroom conditions—children’s enrollment, attendance, and challenging behaviors—mattered for socialization interactions. Teachers at both preschools pursued socialization goals of instilling safe and formal classroom behaviors. At the affluent, majority-White preschool, teachers had a greater capacity to coach children in the moment, and peers had a culture…

Society and law.title: How Sociotropic Aesthetic Judgments Drive Opposition to Dense Housing Development
Society and law.abstract: Voter opposition to dense housing development contributes to America’s housing shortage. Prevailing explanations emphasize homeowner self-interest and “NIMBYism.” We develop a theory of how sociotropic aesthetic judgments shape housing policy preferences and demonstrate its unique implications with a series of descriptive studies and experiments. First, people who choose to live in dense neighborhoods have an aesthetic taste for density, leading homeowners in already-dense areas to be more supportive of dense development both in their neighborhoods and elsewhere. Second, voters are more supportive of dense development when it is proposed in already-dense neighborhoods where it “fits”—even voters who live in those same dense neighborhoods. Finally, genuine aesthetic distaste for tall buildings is widespread and causally affects support for development. Our findings offer a new lens for…

Society and law.title: The Limit of Nature: Thucydides and the Politics of Theory
Society and law.abstract: This article reconsiders Thucydides’s role as a foundational theorist of human nature. Contrary to conventional readings, I argue that Thucydides approaches “nature” ( physis ) less as a universal principle of behavior than as a site of political and theoretical investigation. By distinguishing his authorial voice from those of his speakers, I demonstrate that his analysis consistently approaches human nature as a limit concept—a baseline and boundary of human capacity that emerges in moments of existential precarity—while introducing a more nuanced set of terms to describe the habitual behaviors of political groups. By nevertheless foregrounding the more robust and determinative concept of nature in moments of contentious deliberation, Thucydides encourages reflection on the political dynamics that generate essentialist theories in public discourse. His account thus serves as a…

Society and law.title: The Influence of Police Unions in Local Elections: Evidence from U.S. Cities’ Spending and Performance
Society and law.abstract: Despite growing attention to local policies governing public safety issues, and mounting reports of police union spending to local candidates, the role of police unions in local politics remains understudied. We address this gap by assembling a novel, large-scale dataset on campaign finance in U.S. mayoral elections, covering 2,303 races across 1,073 cities from 2001 to 2019. We document that police unions frequently donate to mayoral candidates—especially in mid-sized and large cities—targeting likely winners and incumbents, and without displaying clear partisan bias. Using a within-city design that accounts for heterogeneous treatment effects in the presence of staggered treatment timing, we find that the election of a police-union-backed mayor leads to an expansion in police department size. However, we do not find improvements in police performance in these cities, suggesting that…

Society and law.title: The Seeds of State Capture: Merit and Patrimonialism in the Colonial Bureaucracy
Society and law.abstract: Bureaucracies vary in the extent to which hiring is meritocratic versus patrimonial. Such outcomes are typically seen as the result of politicians’ behavior. However, politicians often delegate hiring to existing bureaucrats. When political leaders are socially distant from communities they seek to govern and these areas are peripheral to politicians’ core interests, bureaucrats’ private preferences can dominate hiring decisions instead. Colonial and other forms of external state-building typify cases where patrimonialism created by bureaucrats, not politicians, can emerge. Digitizing individual-level records across six decades of British rule in Ghana, we find evidence of patrimonialism rather than meritocracy in the hiring of African staff, with large inequities across ethnic groups. Our results demonstrate the underexplored agency of local bureaucrats in state-building and highlight…

Food industry.title: “Prevalence and associated risk factors of ectoparasite infestation in Ethiopian poultry: meta-analysis”
Food industry.abstract: Ectoparasite infestation is a major parasitic problem affecting chicken health and productivity worldwide. Despite the substantial economic impact of poultry ectoparasites, evidence on their epidemiology in Ethiopia remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of ectoparasite infestation, characterise major ectoparasite groups, and assess associated factors among chickens in Ethiopia. Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2000 and 2026. Seventeen articles met the inclusion criteria, yielding 56 datasets, as some studies reported multiple ectoparasite groups. A random-effects model was used to estimate pooled prevalence while accounting for between-study heterogeneity. The overall pooled prevalence of ectoparasite infestation among…

Food industry.title: Genetic dissection of carcass composition and fat deposition traits in a Pekin duck × Liancheng White duck F₂ population using univariate and cross-trait GWAS
Food industry.abstract: Single-trait and multi-trait genome-wide association studies (C-GWAS) were performed on 18 carcass- and growth-related traits in a Pekin duck × Liancheng White duck F₂ population (n = 242; slaughtered at 70 d) using 12.8 million SNPs. Single-trait GWAS identified major-effect loci for carcass weight and half-eviscerated weight on chromosome 2 (104.68 Mb), for leg muscle weight on chromosome 2 (57.91 Mb), and for abdominal fat weight and skin fat thickness on chromosome 3 (88.46 Mb), revealing heterogeneous genetic architectures ranging from major-effect variants to polygenic backgrounds; the broad signal intervals were consistent with long-range LD in the F₂ population. Food industry.title: Time-resolved multi-omics reveals sustained antiviral activation and hepatic lipid remodeling during ALV-J infection in chickens
Food industry.abstract: Avian leukosis virus subgroup J (ALV-J) is an oncogenic retrovirus associated with persistent infection, immunosuppression, and neoplastic diseases in chickens, with the liver serving as an important target organ. However, the temporal coordination of hepatic immune and metabolic responses during the early course of ALV-J infection remains unclear. Here, we performed time-resolved proteomic and metabolomic analyses of chicken livers at 7, 14, and 21 days post-infection (dpi). Hepatic ALV-J RNA was detected throughout the observation period and was accompanied by histopathological injury and extensive immunometabolic remodeling. Antiviral and interferon-responsive proteins, including OASL, STAT1, EIF2AK2, and CMPK2, remained elevated at multiple time points. The sustained elevation of these antiviral proteins was accompanied by reductions in selected mitochondrial respiratory-chain…

Food industry.title: Lipid nanoparticle–mediated RNA delivery enables protein expression in chicken testes
Food industry.abstract: RNA-lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are emerging tools for poultry vaccination, but methods for local protein expression in reproductive tissues remain underdeveloped. Here, we established RNA delivery to chicken testes using LNPs formulated with the ionizable lipid DLin-MC3-DMA (MC3) and multifocal intratesticular injection through an intercostal surgical approach. Bilateral injections were completed in all six chickens in a surgical-feasibility cohort, with postoperative recovery during the 7-day observation period. At an equal RNA mass dose of 80 µg per testis, conventional messenger RNA (mRNA) encoding enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP) produced detectable reporter signals at days 1, 3, and 7, with the highest measured signal at day 3. An eGFP self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) construct showed delayed detectable expression at days 3 and 7. Delivery of mRNAs encoding CRISPR-associated…

Food industry.title: Enhanced baseline immune priming and controlled inflammation drive resistance to Salmonella Typhimurium in Lueyang Black Chicken
Food industry.abstract: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium is an important foodborne pathogen in poultry, yet the immune mechanisms underlying natural variation in resistance to infection among chicken breeds remain poorly understood. Lueyang Black Chicken (LBC), an indigenous Chinese chicken breed, provides a model for investigating breed-related differences in immune responses to Salmonella infection, although its underlying immune characteristics remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to compare the baseline immune status and immune responses to Salmonella Typhimurium infection between LBC and Arbor Acres broilers (AA), and to explore the potential immunological basis of their differential resistance. A total of 150 LBC and 150 AA were used, and immune cell populations, immune-related gene expression, tissue histopathology, and ileal bacterial loads were assessed under physiological…

Food industry.title: Mixed-species Eimeria challenge depletes circulating fatty acids in laying hens with or without dietary deoxynivalenol exposure
Food industry.abstract: Coccidiosis and deoxynivalenol (DON) can impair intestinal function and nutrient metabolism in poultry. This study investigated the individual and combined effects of mixed-species Eimeria challenge and dietary DON on serum fatty acid (FA) profiles of laying hens. A total of 48 Hy-Line W-36 hens (47 wk of age) were assigned to a 2 × 2 factorial design (n = 6 replicates/treatment): control or DON-contaminated diet (5.70 mg/kg DON) from 47 to 50 wk of age, and oral inoculation with sterile PBS or mixed Eimeria oocysts at 48 wk of age. Serum FA were analyzed by gas chromatography at 6 and 14 d post-inoculation (DPI). Infection was verified by increased gut permeability at 5 DPI (P < 0.001) and intestinal lesions at 6 DPI. Food industry.title: Influence of chromium propionate supplementation on performance of broiler breeder hens during peak production
Food industry.abstract: The objective of this study was to determine the effects of dietary chromium (Cr), as Cr propionate (Cr Prop), on performance and animal safety of broiler breeder hens during peak egg production (wk 31 to 42). Thirty-one-week-old Ross 708 broiler breeder hens (n = 120) were randomly assigned to dietary treatments consisting of 0 (control), 0.2, 0.4, or 0.6 mg supplemental Cr/kg diet. Hens were housed individually and fed once a day with feed offerings equalized across treatments. Egg production was measured daily and eggs were collected on wk 33, 36, 39, and 42 for determination of egg wt, fertility, embryo mortality, and hatchability. Feed intake was similar among treatments and averaged 134 g/d. Body weight gains for the entire study were not affected by treatment. Food industry.title: Essential oils in food preservation: Integrating antimicrobial efficacy with evolutionary and microbiome selectivity considerations
authors: Eliza de Jesus Barros dos Santos
Food industry.abstract: Background Essential oils (EOs) and their constituents (EOCs) can support food preservation, but antimicrobial efficacy alone does not characterize every surviving-cell state or community response. Minimum inhibitory and bactericidal concentrations, colony-forming units, and shelf-life measurements remain essential; additional endpoints may be needed when exposure histories or non-target populations are relevant. Scope and approach This critical narrative review integrates foundational and recent studies on EO/EOC exposure, microbial stress responses, experimental evolution, loss of culturability, and food microbial communities. Evidence is distinguished by intervention, experimental system, exposure design, and endpoint. Food industry.title: Perilla frutescens extract alleviates ovarian oxidative stress in a validated HELP-induced FLHS model through ovarian metabolic reprogramming and cecal microbiome modulation
Food industry.abstract: Perilla frutescens extract (PFE) is rich in bioactive compounds with multiple physiological functions. This study evaluated the effects of dietary PFE on laying performance and ovarian antioxidant capacity in a validated hen model of fatty liver haemorrhagic syndrome (FLHS) induced by a high-energy low-protein (HELP) diet. Hepatic histopathology and biochemical analyses confirmed the successful establishment of the FLHS model. A total of 360 laying hens were randomly assigned to five groups: control, FLHS model, and model supplemented with 200, 400, or 600 mg/kg PFE. The trial consisted of a 2-week adaptation period followed by a 12-week experimental period. Compared with the model group, all PFE treatments significantly increased laying rate, elevated ovarian antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, GSH-Px, CAT, T-AOC), and reduced MDA and AST levels. Food industry.title: Nutrient digestibility and phytate degradation in turkeys fed diets containing a meal from dehulled and ethanol-extracted rapeseed
Food industry.abstract: A rapeseed kernel meal (RKM) was produced by dehulling and ethanol oil extraction. The objective was to determine the prececal digestibility of crude protein (CP) and amino acids (AA) of RKM with and without phytase in turkeys. Digestibility of energy, phosphorus (P), calcium, and phytate disappearance were also determined for the RKM-containing diets. The experiment used a 3 × 2 factorial design with the factors RKM inclusion (0, 12.5, and 25%) and phytase supplementation (0 and 1500 FTU/kg). Turkey hatchlings (B.U.T. 6) were allocated to 42 floor pens in groups of 10, with 7 pens per treatment. The experimental diets were fed from 16 to 21 days of age. The RKM inclusion decreased the prececal digestibility of CP and all AA in the diets ( P < 0.05). Food industry.title: Quercetin and hydroxyapatite nanoparticles modulate developmental, inflammatory, and oxidative responses to lipopolysaccharide in broiler embryos
Food industry.abstract: The effects of quercetin (Q) and hydroxyapatite nanoparticles (HaP NPs) on responses to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) during avian embryogenesis remain unclear. We evaluated the individual and combined effects of Q, HaP NPs, and LPS in a 2 × 2 × 2 factorial in ovo study using 80 Ross 308 eggs (10 per treatment). On embryonic day 14, eggs received 0.2 mL of formulations containing Q and/or HaP NPs (100 µg/mL each) and/or LPS (125 ng/egg); sampling occurred on day 18. Serum biochemistry, serum and hepatic redox-related variables, organ weights, and liver and bursal histomorphometry were assessed. Three-way Q × HaP NPs × LPS interactions were detected for absolute bursal and heart weights (P < 0.001 and P = 0.024, respectively) and serum aspartate aminotransferase activity (P < 0.001). Food industry.title: Emerging strategies in coffee fermentation: From starter culture to synthetic microbial community
Food industry.abstract: Background Coffee is a globally consumed beverage. After harvesting, coffee can be processed in various ways, one of which is the wet method. The conventional wet processing method involves immersing the beans in water for fermentation. Although this fermentation improves the sensory profile of the beverage, the process is generally carried out spontaneously, relying on the indigenous microbiota, which makes standardization difficult. Scope and approach This study employed a narrative review based on articles indexed in scientific databases, including Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect, covering studies published between 2022 and 2026. This study aims to critically analyze conventionally employed fermentation processes and propose the use of synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) as an emerging strategy for this process. Food industry.title: Applications of 16S rRNA gene sequencing for profiling the poultry litter microbiome- an industry perspective
Food industry.abstract: Poultry litter is a dynamic polymicrobial habitat with implications for bird health, food safety, and environmental integrity. Amplicon sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene has emerged as the dominant approach for characterizing poultry-associated microbial communities, offering a scalable and reproducible framework for exploring litter microbial ecology. Complementary to biosurveillance and the expansion of foundational knowledge, 16S-based profiling holds substantial translational value in an industry setting. Microbiome data can inform the identification and mechanistic characterization of pre-, pro-, post-, and synbiotic intervention candidates, including elucidating indirect modes of action mediated through shifts in the native microbial community or litter environment. Food industry.title: Integrated microbiomic and metabolomic analysis reveals key microbes, metabolites, and pathways affecting semen quality in drakes
Food industry.abstract: Semen quality is one of the important indicators for evaluating the reproductive capacity of drakes. Currently, semen quality is one of the main factors limiting the development of artificial insemination technology in ducks. Multiple studies have shown that seminal microorganisms are important factors affecting duck semen quality via metabolites, but the specific mechanisms remain unclear. Therefore, this study used 340-day-old Nonghua drakes as experimental subjects. After routine semen quality evaluation of the 86 drakes, we found large individual differences in semen quality. Then, 8 drakes with the highest and lowest SQF were divided into high semen quality (HSQ) and low semen quality (LSQ) groups. Food industry.title: Effect of photoperiod on hypothalamic GnIH expression in broilers
Food industry.abstract: Poultry are highly sensitive to photoperiod, and light critically regulates numerous physiological and behavioral processes in birds. This study examined the effects of varying photoperiods on hypothalamic gonadotropin-inhibitory hormone (GnIH) expression in broilers. A total of 45 healthy male broilers at 0 days of age were selected and randomly assigned to three photoperiod groups: A (16L:8D), B (12L:12D), and C (8L:16D). Each experimental group was housed in separate rooms containing five birds per cage, three cages per group. Hypothalamic tissue samples were collected at 14 days of age (P14). Immunohistochemical staining was employed to quantify GnIH-immunoreactive (-ir) cells in the hypothalamus. Food industry.title: Embryonic thermal manipulation affects early post-hatch growth and hepatic transcriptomic responses in Jinding ducklings
Food industry.abstract: Embryonic thermal manipulation is a well-established strategy for regulating early growth, development, and metabolism in poultry, while research on the late embryonic stages, a period of rapid yolk lipid mobilization, remains limited. Here, Jinding duck (Anas platyrhynchos domesticus) embryos were exposed to mild heating (+1°C relative to the control group) during late incubation. Post-hatch growth, serum lipid profiles, thyroid hormone levels, and hepatic transcriptomes were examined in the ducklings. Embryos given moderate thermal conditioning on day 21 (MTC-21, short-term) produced ducklings with longer tarsi than controls on post-hatch days 3-6, whereas those given MTC-14 (long-term) showed no difference in tarsus length from controls. Food industry.title: Plant-based cheese alternatives: Reframing processing strategies towards fermentation-driven innovation
Food industry.abstract: Background The growing demand for sustainable and animal-free foods has accelerated global interest in plant-based cheese alternatives (PBCAs). Despite rapid market expansion, many commercial PBCA products still struggle to replicate the flavour, texture and functionality of dairy cheese. Key barriers include difficulty forming meltable plant protein networks, limited utilisation of plant-derived sugars by some starter cultures and a lack of suitable precursors for cheese-like flavour development. Scope and approach This review presents a process-based perspective on PBCA development by categorising current approaches into non-fermented and fermented systems. Food industry.title: Dietary allicin supplementation alleviates intestinal injury in broilers challenged with an Eimeria vaccine
Food industry.abstract: Allicin (AL) possesses antibacterial, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory properties. However, reports on its effect against coccidial infection in broilers are limited. The objective of this study was to investigate the effects of dietary allicin supplementation on the growth performance and intestinal health of broilers challenged with coccidia. A total of 300 healthy male Cobb broilers with uniform body weight were randomly assigned to five treatment groups: negative control (NC), positive control (PC), AL50, AL100, and AL200. Each group had 6 replicates with 10 broilers per replicate. The NC and PC groups were fed a basal diet, while the AL50, AL100, and AL200 groups were fed the basal diet supplemented with 50, 100, and 200 mg/kg allicin, respectively. Food industry.title: Prevalence and levels of mycotoxins in poultry feed and ingredients: a global systematic review and meta-analysis
Food industry.abstract: Mycotoxins are a global concern due to their widespread occurrence throughout the food chain and their potential risks to human and animal health. This study investigated the global prevalence and concentrations of mycotoxins in poultry feed and its components, assessing their potential health implication. Following the PRISMA methodology, 78 articles were included, with data processed (outlier removal) and analysed using STATA®. Globally, fumonisins B1 (FB1) and B2 (FB2) were the most prevalent (70% and 68%), with concentrations of 1,159 µg kg –1 and 164 µg kg –1 , respectively. Food industry.title: Guanidinoacetic acid supplementation in broiler chickens fed standard or reduced metabolizable energy diets: effects on performance, gut health, antioxidant status, and meat quality
Food industry.abstract: Reducing dietary metabolizable energy (ME) may compromise broiler performance. Guanidinoacetic acid (GAA), a creatine precursor, may support performance under reduced-ME feeding, although its associated effects on tissue oxidative status and meat quality warrant investigation. A 35-d trial investigated these responses in 560 Ross 308 broilers allocated to five dietary treatments: standard ME (T1), T1 + 0.06% GAA (T2), reduced ME (-80 kcal/kg; T3), T3 + 0.06% GAA (T4), and T3 + 0.09% GAA (T5). T3 impaired starter growth, whereas GAA supplementation restored starter performance. During d24-35, performance differed among treatments (P < 0.05); T2 and T5 had higher BW and ADG than T3, and T3 had higher FCR than all other treatments. Food industry.title: Plasma-based technologies for aquatic product preservation: Balancing microbial control and oxidative deterioration
Food industry.abstract: : Background Aquatic products are highly nutritious but are particularly susceptible to microbial contamination, lipid oxidation, and protein degradation during postharvest handling and storage, posing challenges to food safety, quality preservation, and sustainable cold-chain logistics. Atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) and plasma-activated liquids (PALs), particularly plasma-activated water (PAW), have emerged as promising non-thermal preservation technologies because they generate reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) capable of inactivating microorganisms while minimizing thermal damage. Food industry.title: Dietary Inotodiol alleviates AFB1-induced intestinal injury in Leizhou black ducks via modulation of NF-κB/p62/Nrf2 signaling pathway
Food industry.abstract: Aflatoxin B 1 (AFB 1 ) is a highly hazardous mycotoxin that poses serious threats to poultry health, production performance, and food safety. Inotodiol (INO), a bioactive triterpenoid extracted from the medicinal fungus Inonotus obliquus , exhibits well-established anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. However, its protective efficacy against AFB 1 -induced intestinal injury in ducks and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. A total of 42 healthy 2-day-old Leizhou black ducks were used. After a 7-day acclimatization period, the ducks were randomly assigned to one of six groups: basal diet (control), basal diet+AFB 1 (AFB 1 ), basal diet+AFB 1 +0.005% INO (AFB 1 +INO-1), basal diet+AFB 1 +0.015% INO (AFB 1 +INO-2), basal diet+AFB1+0.015% resveratrol (AFB 1 +RES), and basal diet+INO (INO). Food industry.title: The effect of in ovo treatments with galactooligosaccharide and sodium butyrate on microbiota activity and mucosal proteome in the ileum and cecum of broiler chickens
Food industry.abstract: The study aimed to determine the effect of in ovo stimulation with galactooligosaccharide (GOS) and sodium butyrate (SB) on the intestinal microbiota activity, epigenetic events, and mucosal protein profiles in the ileum and cecum of broiler chickens. The experiment was conducted on 1,068 fertilized eggs of Ross 308 hens, divided into four groups: negative control (NC) and three in ovo-treated, each of 267 eggs. On the 12th day of incubation, 0.2 ml NaCl without addition (positive control, PC), with 3.5 mg GOS or with 0.6 mg SB were injected into egg air chambers. After hatching at day 21, males were selected for a 42-day rearing. Then, ileal and cecal digesta and mucosal samples (n = 10 per group) were taken for analyses. Food industry.title: Effects of different Eimeria maxima infection doses on growth performance and gut and bone health in a dual-infection model of necrotic enteritis in layer chicks
Food industry.abstract: Necrotic enteritis (NE) is an enteric disease that causes approximately 6 billion USD in annual losses to the global poultry industry. Although NE has been extensively studied in broiler chickens, limited information is available regarding NE in layers. Therefore, this study evaluated the effects of different doses of E. maxima (EM) on growth performance, intestinal health, and bone parameters in a dual infection model of NE in layer chicks. A total of 300 twenty-one-day old Hy-Line W-36 pullet chicks were randomly allocated into five treatments with six replicates of 10 birds each: (1) NC, non-challenged control; (2) CP, Clostridium perfringens control; (3) EM10K+CP; (4) EM20K+CP; and (5) EM40K+CP. Birds in the EM10K+CP, EM20K+CP, and EM40K+CP groups received 10,000, 20,000, and 40,000 sporulated E. maxima oocysts respectively on 0 days post-inoculation (DPI), whereas the CP and all…

Food industry.title: The role of selenoprotein O in alleviating intestinal inflammation with nano-selenium: A perspective based on pyroptosis and macrophage polarization crosstalk
Food industry.abstract: Terbuthylazine (Ter) can induce excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, triggering intestinal damage. During this pathological process, macrophages undergo M1 polarization to drive inflammatory progression. As a highly efficient Se source, Nano-selenium (Nano-Se) has been proven to possess excellent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory features. Therefore, this study aims to investigate whether Nano-Se alleviates Ter-induced intestinal injury and elucidate its specific mechanism. Broilers, CSIEC and HD11 cells were treated with Ter or/and Nano-Se. We also constructed a selenoprotein O (SelO) overexpression model in CSIEC and HD11 cells to explore the specific mechanism. Integrated network toxicology and bioinformatics analyses revealed the involvement of Ter in oxidative stress, macrophage polarization, metabolism, pyroptosis, and inflammation process.…

Food industry.title: Chicoric acid alleviates LPS-induced hepatic inflammation in broilers by regulating the TLR4/MAPK signaling pathway
Food industry.abstract: Chicoric acid (CA) is a natural phenolic acid with well-documented anti-inflammatory properties. This study systematically evaluated the protective effects and underlying mechanisms of CA against lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced hepatic inflammation in broilers. Network pharmacology analysis identified 277 overlapping genes associated with hepatic inflammation, and functional enrichment revealed significant involvement of the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway. Molecular docking suggested potential stable interactions between CA and core targets, including TLR4, transforming growth factor-β-activated kinase 1 (TAK1), c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK), and p38 MAPK. Food industry.title: Heat stress and avian pathogenic Escherichia coli infection differentially alter bacterial colonization dynamics, mucosal and systemic immunity, and cecal microbiome homeostasis in late-production laying hens in cage-free housing
Food industry.abstract: Heat stress (HS) and avian pathogenic E. coli (APEC) infection are major challenges to the health and productivity of commercial laying hens, yet their combined effects remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of continuous HS and oral APEC O78 infection on production performance, bacterial colonization, immune responses, and the cecal microbiome of 70-week-old Hy-Line W-36 cage-free laying hens. Food industry.abstract: Skeletal muscle development is a major determinant of poultry meat production, yet the stage-specific regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, pectoral muscle samples from eight developmental stages of chickens (E9-E18, D1, D7) were subjected to transcriptome sequencing, with two representative stages (E9 and D1) further analyzed through integrative whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS), chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq), and high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) to investigate epigenetic and chromatin structural regulation. Food industry.title: Hydrogen-dependent sulfur and iron reduction by marine thermophiles as analogs for early Earth and ocean world processes
Food industry.abstract: Life on the early Earth was likely anaerobic, H 2 dependent, CO 2 fixing, and thermophilic in a marine hydrothermal setting. Geochemical and mineral evidence suggests that sulfur and iron respiration occurred during the Paleoarchean (3.6–3.2 Ga). However, the predominant mechanisms of H 2 -dependent sulfur and iron respiration in hydrothermal systems, then or now, have yet to be elucidated. Studying these processes in microorganisms from modern hydrothermal systems provides context for interpreting the characteristics of life during the Paleoarchaean. All the bacteria and archaea that have been cultured and characterized as extremely thermophilic, marine, H 2 dependent, and sulfur reducing or iron reducing (36 species) were surveyed for genes related to energy generation and terminal reduction processes. Food industry.title: Regulatory governance and full-scale digital transformation for prediction-based food safety management: Global trends and future perspectives
Food industry.abstract: Background The global food safety paradigm is shifting from traditional, reactive hazard control toward proactive, predictive risk management to address increasingly complex supply chain vulnerabilities. However, current digital implementations remain fragmented, creating structural bottlenecks that hinder the transition to next-generation regulatory science. Food industry.abstract: Avian eggshell pores connect embryonic respiration, water balance, microbial defense and egg quality, but the evidence is distributed across physiological and production disciplines. We combined quantitative literature mapping with biological synthesis. We assembled a query-defined corpus of 445 publications from Web of Science and Scopus searches, including taxonomically relaxed and structure-function searches. Species-masked title-abstract text was analyzed by non-negative matrix factorization, with five topics retained for interpretation. Controlled dictionaries supplied complementary species, function, structure and technology annotations. Food industry.abstract: Methanogens are responsible for producing approximately one billion metric tons of methane each year within Earth’s anaerobic environments as a byproduct of their energy metabolism. They play a vital role in the global carbon cycle. There are three main pathways for methanogenesis: hydrogenotrophic, which uses H 2 and CO 2 to produce methane; methylotrophic, which utilizes methylated compounds like methanol and amines; and aceticlastic, which converts acetate into methane and CO 2 . Instead of substrate-level ATP production, methanogens conserve energy through a membrane-bound electron transport chain and flavin-based electron bifurcation (FBEB). Food industry.abstract: Eggshell quality is an important economic trait in egg-laying poultry. As a cytoplasmic soluble calcium-binding protein, CALB1 (Calbindin-D28k) binds Ca²⁺, modulates calcium ion transport and mediates diverse calcium-related physiological processes. Food industry.title: Sustainable 2-keto-L-gulonic acid biosynthesis via single-strain one-step fermentation
Food industry.abstract: L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is an essential antioxidant molecule that maintains normal physiological functions in humans. Currently, industrial production relies primarily on a three-strain, two-step fermentation process to produce 2-keto-L-gulonic acid (2-KLG), the direct precursor of vitamin C. 2-KLG is then converted to vitamin C through chemical lactonization. However, this process is limited by prolonged fermentation cycles, poor stability of the mixed-culture system, and complex process control. In recent years, engineered single-strain platforms capable of one-step 2-KLG biosynthesis have emerged as a promising strategy for more sustainable vitamin C production. Food industry.abstract: One-hundred and twenty 31-wk-old broiler breeder hens (Ross 708) were used to evaluate the effects of dietary chromium (Cr), as Cr propionate (Cr Prop), on metabolic responses associated with insulin action. Plasma glucose and nonesterified fatty acid (NEFA), and liver glycogen concentrations were used as indicators of insulin sensitivity. Hens were randomly assigned to dietary treatments consisting of 0 (control), 0.20, 0.40, or 0.60 mg supplemental Cr/kg diet, and were housed individually. Food industry.abstract: Protocatechuic acid (PCA) possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. This study aimed to investigate the effects of PCA on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammatory responses in HD11 cells and its potential mechanisms of action. The regulatory effects of PCA on LPS-induced inflammatory responses were systematically evaluated by detecting nitric oxide (NO), reactive oxygen species (ROS), inflammation-related factors, and protein expression, combined with transcriptomic sequencing analysis. Food industry.title: Impact of arsenic exposure on the gut-microbiota-liver axis in poultry
Food industry.abstract: Arsenic (As), a priority hazardous substance widely distributed in nature, endangers poultry health and food safety. The gut‑microbiota‑liver axis forms a bidirectional regulatory network, with the intestine acting as the main absorption site and the liver as the key metabolic‑detoxification organ for As. This review summarizes arsenic‑induced toxic injuries to this axis in poultry. Food industry.abstract: Mycoplasma gallisepticum and Salmonella Gallinarum (SG) are economically important bacterial pathogens affecting poultry production, yet no single vaccine addresses both pathogens simultaneously. We engineered a recombinant SG vaccine strain, JOL3203, based on the dual-expression plasmid pJHL270, incorporating functionally distinct prokaryotic and eukaryotic cassettes to deliver two complementary Mycoplasma gallisepticum antigens from a single immunization regimen.
